title.title: The near-boundary Birkhoff conjecture
title.subtitle: Claim: a smooth convex billiard with a continuous collar of caustics at its boundary is an ellipse

beats.text: A caustic is a curve that billiard trajectories stay tangent to
An ellipse has a full collar of them next to its boundary: confocal ellipses
Claim: a continuous collar like this forces the table to be an ellipse

achievement.label: Birkhoff conjecture (1927), near-boundary form
achievement.context: Before: only near ellipses (Avila–De Simoi–Kaloshin 2016; Kaloshin–Sorrentino 2018)
achievement.note: Not the full conjecture: the Cantor family of caustics KAM gives does not count

plain: On a curved pool table, if paths near the rim all hug neat nested loops, the table must be an ellipse

steps: Twist inequalities force the invariant curves to be neat graphs
Bouncing chains then force the boundary to be analytic
A companion paper shows the table must be an ellipse

boxes: analytic boundary and collar of caustics

voice.text: Bouncing paths in an ellipse keep touching nested curves, a whole collar near the edge.
First the curves become graphs, then the edge becomes analytic, then an ellipse.
Claimed: only the ellipse has such a collar.
